However, he can knock you away with Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption if you get too close, so have a way to finish him ready.
Velkoz.fight: Usually, poke with Lux E Lucent Singularity, then use a basic attack to consume Lux P Illumination’s mark. Don’t use Lux Q Light Binding to poke; save it for a chance to bind Vel’Koz and finish him when Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down. If you start getting hit by Vel’Koz’s abilities in succession, back away instead of continuing the fight.
Velkoz.laning: Lux has no mobility, so play at the edge of your range and first check bushes you have no vision of with Lux E Lucent Singularity. When pulling the wave, hit only Vel’Koz with Lux E Lucent Singularity and don’t hit minions. Lux E Lucent Singularity costs a lot of mana, so don’t cast it on cooldown.
Velkoz.phase: Early on, Lux can set up a kill by hitting Lux Q Light Binding, but don’t let Vel’Koz land repeated poke. In the late game, prioritize positioning over damage and keep enough distance to dodge Vel’Koz’s abilities.
Velkoz.teamfight: Stay behind your frontline, stop engages with Lux Q Light Binding, block paths with Lux E Lucent Singularity, and throw Lux W Prismatic Barrier toward your grouped allies. When Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray begins, first look for an angle to interrupt it with Lux Q Light Binding. Use Lux R Final Spark when you can pierce multiple enemies in a line or secure a clear takedown.
Velkoz.watch: You also have to dodge the split beams from Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission, so don’t only move sideways; move toward Vel’Koz or behind where the beams passed. If repeated hits build stacks of Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction, back away to let the stacks expire. When Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray begins, first look for an angle to interrupt it with Lux Q Light Binding.

Yasuo.build: Yasuo’s main damage is physical and Lux has low armor, so build armor first. Early on, buy Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps. If the enemy team has an assassin, get Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier.
Yasuo.combo: When Yasuo W Wind Wall disappears or you have an angle around it, root him with Lux Q Light Binding. Then, while Lux E Lucent Singularity is placed, cast Lux R Final Spark, followed by basic attack → detonate Lux E Lucent Singularity → basic attack to consume the Lux P Illumination mark.
Yasuo.escape: Right after Yasuo throws his tornado, Yasuo Q Steel Tempest stacks reset, so look for a chance to engage. Don’t go in immediately just because Yasuo E Sweeping Blade alone is down; look for an opening with crowd control before Yasuo R Last Breath is ready again. Land Lux Q Light Binding then so he can’t escape.
Yasuo.fight: First, poke off Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield before trading serious damage. Place and detonate Lux E Lucent Singularity, then use a basic attack to consume the Lux P Illumination mark, but save Lux Q Light Binding until you can stop Yasuo’s engage or set up a kill. Right after Yasuo throws his tornado, he won’t have a knock-up available for a while, so look for a chance to attack.
Yasuo.laning: Play at the edge of your range and watch out for Yasuo E Sweeping Blade, which he uses to dash through minions. Keep the wave thin and pushed toward your side to reduce the minions Yasuo can use to approach. Lux E Lucent Singularity costs a lot of mana, so don’t cast it repeatedly without reason, and throw it to check a bush you have no vision of before entering.
Yasuo.phase: Early on, Lux can set up a kill by landing Lux Q Light Binding, but if Yasuo gets on you, it’s difficult to escape on your own, so prioritize keeping your distance. Lux’s burst grows strong as she builds ability power through the mid and late game, but in the late game, positioning so Yasuo can’t catch you matters more than damage.
Yasuo.teamfight: From behind your frontline, stop Yasuo’s engage with Lux Q Light Binding and block paths with Lux E Lucent Singularity. Cast Lux W Prismatic Barrier toward your grouped allies to block damage. Use Lux R Final Spark to hit grouped enemies in a line or secure a certain kill.
Yasuo.watch: Yasuo E Sweeping Blade uses minions to approach Lux, so keep your distance where there are many minions. After Yasuo lands Yasuo Q Steel Tempest twice, his next tornado can knock you up, so watch the sound and effects and sidestep out of its line. When Yasuo W Wind Wall appears, save Lux Q Light Binding and go around the wall or wait for it to disappear.

Zyra.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Zyra deals mostly magic damage and Lux has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Zyra.combo: When Zyra E Grasping Roots is down and you have a chance to land Lux Q Light Binding, use Q → place Lux E Lucent Singularity and hold it → Lux R Final Spark → basic attack → detonate E → basic attack. Delay the E detonation so two basic attacks consume the Lux P Illumination mark. Lux R has a cast delay, so chain it before the Q root wears off.
Zyra.escape: Right after you dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots and it is down, you have a chance to go in. Zyra has no mobility, so close the distance from the side without plants, then catch her with Lux Q Light Binding. If you see the indicator for Zyra R Stranglethorns, prioritize getting outside its area over chasing.
Zyra.fight: After dodging Zyra E Grasping Roots, poke with Lux E Lucent Singularity where there are no plants, then use a basic attack to consume the Lux P Illumination mark. When Zyra E is down, root her with Lux Q Light Binding to set up a kill. Lux Q is also a way to stop a counterattack, so don’t use it for light poke.
Zyra.laning: Move at the edge of your range to dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots, and briefly back off from areas where plants have accumulated. Step on seeds as you pass, but move back when Zyra uses an ability, then step on them again. Check bushes where you have no vision with Lux E Lucent Singularity, and when holding the wave near your side, make sure E doesn’t hit minions.
Zyra.phase: Early on, Lux can set up a kill by landing Lux Q Light Binding, but keep your distance so Zyra E Grasping Roots doesn’t catch you. In the late game, positioning matters more than Lux’s damage, so don’t fight where Zyra has built up seeds and plants.
Zyra.teamfight: From behind your frontline, stop Zyra’s engage with Lux Q Light Binding, block paths with Lux E Lucent Singularity, and cast Lux W Prismatic Barrier toward your grouped allies. Avoid areas where Zyra has held her ground for a long time, and move the fight to make her accumulated seeds useless. Use Lux R Final Spark when you can hit several enemies in a line or secure a certain kill.
Zyra.watch: If you’re rooted by Zyra E Grasping Roots, it can lead into plant damage and even the knock-up from Zyra R Stranglethorns. Move sideways at the edge of your range to dodge E, and walk outside the area as soon as you see the R indicator. Don’t fight where her plants have gathered.
